# Articulation and technique

Pitches are MIDI numbers, 60 = middle C. Onsets are slots 0 to 15 of a sixteenth grid, so slot 4 is beat 2; lengths are in beats. Tiers: M1 is needed in a first test set, M2 has one or two sources or is a jazz or world idiom, M3 is single-source, inferred or theory only. Tags: `source states`, `measured`, `derived` (our computation on public data), `inferred` (our reading), `snippet` (a search excerpt), `single source`, `proposal` (a policy, not a fact). Source ids are listed in `dictionary/sources.json`.

| staccato | `articulation.staccato` | sounding length 0.25 to 0.5 of the grid step | Short and detached: about 50 percent of the grid step (0.125 beat on sixteenths). Staccatissimo goes down to 33 or 25 percent. In the note list the share is the gate. | M1 | source states | guides |
| tenuto | `articulation.tenuto` | sounding length 1 to 1 of the grid step | Held for the whole grid step, 100 percent of the step. | M1 | source states | guides |
| portato | `articulation.portato` | sounding length 0.67 to 0.75 of the grid step | Between staccato and tenuto: 67 or 75 percent of the step. Sources disagree on the figure. | M2 | source states | guides |

| glide (slide) | `articulation.glide` | the next note starts at least 5 ms before this one ends | Slide from one pitch to the next by overlapping the two notes. The preset needs mono mode, legato on and a portamento time above zero. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |
| 303 slide | `articulation.303-slide` | the next note starts at least 5 ms before this one ends | A flagged acid step glides into the next, and the slide gate starts one step later. Slide only 15 to 35 percent of the notes. Glide time is 60 to 120 ms. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |
| 303 accent | `articulation.303-accent` | velocity 100 to 127 | An accented acid step: velocity 100 to 127 against 70 to 90 for the rest. The preset must send velocity to level and cutoff, or the accent is silent. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |
| 808 slide | `articulation.808-slide` | the next note starts at least 5 ms before this one ends | A mono 808 glide: the end of one note overlaps the next and the notes run long. Glide time is 80 to 150 ms, fast 30 to 50 ms, slow 200 ms and more. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |

## Bass techniques

| Word | Id | Rule | Meaning | Tier | Tag | Sources |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| root notes | `bass.root-notes` | tonic: the first or last phrase note, or the held bass, is the root | The bass plays the chord root. Psytrance sits at pitches 29 to 33 and rolling techno at 43. | M1 | source states | guides |
| offbeat bass | `bass.offbeat-bass` | bass at 2 6 10 14 | Bass on the eighth offbeats, slots 2, 6, 10 and 14, with notes of 0.25 to 0.5 beat. Melodic techno alternates velocity 100 and 85, with a ghost at slot 15 at 60 to 70. | M1 | source states | guides |
| rolling, sense `grid`, default | `bass.rolling.grid` | kick at 0 4 8 12; bass at 1 2 3 5 6 7 9 10 11 13 14 15 | The psytrance and techno bass grid: kick on every beat and a bass note on each other sixteenth, 12 per bar on one pitch. Notes are equal in velocity, 0.125 to 0.19 beat long (gate 60) and never legato. | M1 | source states | guides |
| rolling, sense `dnb` | `bass.rolling.dnb` | none | In drum and bass, either a busy top loop under simple drums or a busy mid bass over a steady sub. It has no note grid. | M2 | source states | guides |
| rolling, sense `hat-roll` | `bass.rolling.hat-roll` | none | A trap hat roll: repeated hi-hat hits that rise in velocity into the snare. See the named rhythm hat roll. | M2 | source states | guides |
| root-fifth (root and fifth) | `bass.root-fifth` | tones 0 7 | The bass plays the root, then the note seven semitones above it. | M2 | source states | guides |
| walking bass | `bass.walking-bass` | bass at 0 4 8 12 | One note per beat, slots 0, 4, 8 and 12, each 0.9 to 1.0 beat. Beat 1 is the root, beat 3 a chord tone, and beat 4 an approach note a semitone from the next root. A pitch is not repeated twice in a row. | M2 | source states | guides |
| pedal bass (pedal) | `bass.pedal-bass` | at least 100 % of bars repeat an earlier bar; for at least 4 bars | One bass pitch held or repeated for 4 or more bars while the chords above change. | M2 | source states | guides |
| sub following the kick | `bass.sub-following-the-kick` | none | The bass onsets equal the kick onsets, as in 808, trap and dubstep. House and techno do the opposite and play in the gaps. No single note rule relates two parts. | M2 | source states | guides |
| reese | `bass.reese` | sounding length at least 1 beats | A detuned, growling bass whose notes last 1 beat or more. | M2 | inferred | lexicon |
| wobble | `bass.wobble` | sounding length 1 to 4 beats | A bass whose filter is moved by a fast LFO. The rate is a preset matter. In MIDI it is one sustained note per phrase, 1 to 4 beats long. | M2 | source states | guides |

## Lead and phrase techniques

| Word | Id | Rule | Meaning | Tier | Tag | Sources |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| hook | `lead.hook` | 2 to 6 notes per bar | The catchy short melody, a lead of 2 to 6 distinct pitches over 1 to 2 bars, repeated. An uplifting trance motif has 4 to 6 notes over 8 bars. | M1 | source states | guides |
| riff | `lead.riff` | changes every 2 bars, on bars 1 + k times that | A short repeating figure of 1 to 2 bars. | M2 | source states | guides |
| ostinato | `lead.ostinato` | at least 100 % of bars repeat an earlier bar; for at least 4 bars | The same pitches and rhythm repeated for 4 or more bars. | M2 | source states | guides |
| call and response (call-and-response) | `lead.call-and-response` | tonic: the first or last phrase note, or the held bass, is the root | Two phrases of equal length. The first ends off the tonic, on the 2nd, 5th or flat 7th, and the second ends on the root. | M2 | source states | guides |
| fill | `lead.fill` | none | The last beat or bar of a 4 or 8 bar phrase gets denser, such as a snare roll that speeds up and rises in velocity. | M2 | source states | guides |
| lead swoop | `lead.swoop` | the next note starts at least 5 ms before this one ends | A long, slow glide into a lead note, 150 to 300 ms, by overlapping the notes. | M3 | inferred | lexicon |

## Arpeggios

| Word | Id | Rule | Meaning | Tier | Tag | Sources |
| :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- |
| arpeggio (arpeggiated) | `arp.arpeggio` | up, 0.25 beats per step | The notes of a chord played one at a time, sorted by pitch, one per step. A step of 1/8 is 0.5 beat, 1/16 is 0.25 and 1/16T is 0.1667. Gate is a share of the step. | M1 | source states | guides |
| arp up (up arp) | `arp.arp-up` | up, 0.25 beats per step | The chord notes climb from low to high, then start again. | M1 | source states | guides |
| arp down (down arp) | `arp.arp-down` | down, 0.25 beats per step | The chord notes fall from high to low, then start again. | M1 | source states | guides |
| arp up-down (arp up and down, up-down arp) | `arp.arp-up-down` | up and down, 0.25 beats per step | Up, then down. The period is 2N-2 steps for N chord notes without repeated end notes, and 2N with them. Manuals differ. | M2 | source states | guides |
| trance arp | `arp.trance-arp` | degrees 1 3 5 8 5 3, 0.25 beats per step, gate 60 to 70 % | The trance pattern: root, 3rd, 5th, octave, 5th, 3rd. Six notes realign with the bar every 3 bars. Gate is 60 to 70 percent of the step. | M2 | single source | guides |

In MIDI, sustain full-bar chords and leave slot mod 4 of 0 empty in the bass. The first bass note after the kick may be 30 percent quieter or 5 to 15 ms later. | M2 | source states | guides |
| trance gate (gate) | `pad.trance-gate` | sounding length at least 4 beats | A chopped pad. In MIDI it is one held chord. An LFO or step pattern on volume makes the chop, 16 steps per bar at 136 to 140 BPM. | M2 | source states | guides |
